x: The Guntur famine of 1832-33 (Dokkala or Nandana Karuvu) was the worst famine in the south, killing about 2 lakh people, roughly half the population. Option A describes the 1866 Kurnool famine (40% of the district died), and C describes the Ganjam famine after the American Civil War.

The Kurnool famine was in 1866, when 40% of the district died. The other pairs are wrong: the Great Famine was 1876-78 (1832-33 is the Guntur famine), the Guntur famine was 1832-33 (1791-92 is the Northern Circars or Ganjam famine), and 1876-78 is the Great Famine, not a Northern Circars famine.

The Chalisa famine of 1783-84 struck North India (Delhi, Awadh, Punjab). The other pairs are wrong: Doji Bara was 1791-92 in the Deccan, Hyderabad and the Northern Circars (Bengal 1770 is the Great Bengal Famine); the 1943 Bengal famine is not the 'Great Famine' (that name belongs to 1876-78 and 1896-97); and the Orissa famine was 1865-66 (1899-1900 hit west and central India).
